question: What is the primary purpose of applying management functions in nursing?

options.B: To achieve organizational goals efficiently and effectively
options.C: To replace clinical duties with administrative paperwork
options.D: To reduce the number of patients admitted to a ward

explanation: Management in nursing focuses on achieving organizational goals efficiently and effectively through coordinated efforts. [learn more](GST321_U1_T4#GST321_U1_T4_h1)

question: Who do nurse managers typically act as a crucial link between?

options.B: Hospital administration and bedside clinical staff

explanation: Nurse managers serve as a crucial bridge connecting higher hospital administration with the bedside clinical staff. [learn more](GST321_U1_T4#GST321_U1_T4_h1)

question: Which management function is considered foundational for nursing management?
explanation: Planning is the foundational function of nursing management as it determines goals and strategies before other actions occur. [learn more](GST321_U1_T4#GST321_U1_T4_h2)

question: Why are standard operating procedures (SOPs) and protocols important outputs of planning?

options.B: They provide clear, evidence-based guidelines for clinical interventions
options.C: They eliminate the need for nursing education
options.D: They restrict nurses from making any independent decisions

explanation: Protocols and SOPs provide clear, evidence-based instructions for safe clinical interventions like medication administration and infection control. [learn more](GST321_U1_T4#GST321_U1_T4_h2)

question: What is the primary purpose of organizing in a nursing unit?

options.A: To translate set goals into a structured framework of roles and workflows
options.B: To punish staff who fail to meet deadlines
options.C: To increase the duration of nursing shifts
options.D: To eliminate the need for shift handovers

explanation: Organizing establishes a structured framework of roles, workflows, and responsibilities to achieve planned goals. [learn more](GST321_U1_T4#GST321_U1_T4_h3)

question: How does clear role structuring benefit a nursing unit?

options.B: It reduces role ambiguity and prevents task duplication
options.D: It stops all communication between staff

explanation: Clearly defining responsibilities prevents overlapping duties and reduces confusion among staff members regarding who should perform specific tasks. [learn more](GST321_U1_T4#GST321_U1_T4_h3)

question: What does patient allocation involve in nursing management?

options.A: Matching patient clinical acuity with the skill level of the nurse
options.B: Assigning patients randomly to any available bed
options.C: Choosing which patients receive hospital bills
options.D: Determining how many doctors work in a ward

explanation: Patient allocation matches the complexity of patient care needs with the appropriate competency level of available nursing staff. [learn more](GST321_U1_T4#GST321_U1_T4_h4)

question: Why is strategic staffing particularly critical in many Nigerian healthcare settings?

options.A: There is an excess of registered nurses
options.B: Nurse-to-patient ratios often exceed international recommendations due to workforce shortages
options.D: Patients prefer not to be nursed by professionals

explanation: Workforce shortages and high nurse-to-patient ratios make strategic staffing essential to maintain safe care delivery. [learn more](GST321_U1_T4#GST321_U1_T4_h4)

question: What is the primary focus of the directing function in nursing management?

options.B: Guiding, inspiring, and overseeing nursing staff to accomplish objectives
options.C: Calculating the monthly budget for medications
options.D: Recruiting new doctors for the clinic

explanation: Directing involves active leadership, motivation, and supervision to guide staff toward achieving unit and institutional goals. [learn more](GST321_U1_T4#GST321_U1_T4_h5)

question: Why is bidirectional communication important in the directing phase?

options.A: It ensures staff understand directives and can report clinical concerns safely
options.B: It eliminates the need for written patient records
options.D: It prevents patients from speaking to doctors

explanation: Open, two-way communication ensures clear understanding of instructions and encourages staff to report safety concerns without fear. [learn more](GST321_U1_T4#GST321_U1_T4_h5)

question: What is the primary purpose of the controlling function in nursing management?

options.A: To monitor performance and evaluate outcomes against established standards
options.B: To dictate what staff wear to work

explanation: Controlling involves monitoring performance, comparing it against established standards, and implementing corrective actions. [learn more](GST321_U1_T4#GST321_U1_T4_h6)

question: What should a nurse manager do when performance falls below expected clinical standards?

options.A: Ignore the issue until a patient complains
options.B: Investigate root causes and implement corrective actions
options.C: Immediately dismiss the entire nursing team
options.D: Hide the data from hospital administration

explanation: Effective controlling requires investigating the root causes of deviations and taking corrective measures like retraining or protocol revision. [learn more](GST321_U1_T4#GST321_U1_T4_h6)

question: Why is coordination essential in multi-disciplinary healthcare teams?

options.A: It ensures all team members are synchronized to prevent fragmented care
options.B: It allows nurses to take over the roles of physicians
options.C: It removes the need for patient documentation
options.D: It increases the time patients spend waiting for medication

explanation: Coordination synchronizes the efforts of various healthcare professionals, eliminating fragmented care and clinical errors. [learn more](GST321_U1_T4#GST321_U1_T4_h7)

question: What does decision-making involve within a multi-disciplinary healthcare team?

options.A: Making all clinical choices independently without consulting others
options.B: Gathering relevant data, weighing options, and choosing the best course of action
options.C: Leaving all critical choices to hospital accountants
options.D: Avoiding difficult clinical choices until emergencies happen

explanation: Decision-making requires reviewing clinical data, evaluating options, and selecting the optimal course of action for patient care. [learn more](GST321_U1_T4#GST321_U1_T4_h7)
